values.note: $20 a night, with the fee and registration procedure posted at the campground kiosk. A Recreation Passport is required for vehicle entry to every state forest campground.

fees.source: https://www.michigan.gov/recsearch/sfcampgroundsa-m/bigknob ('Overnight fees ($20 for most sites) and registration procedures are posted at the information kiosk at each campground') + https://www.michigan.gov/dnr/things-to-do/camping-and-lodging/state-forest-campgrounds/amenity-table (nightly fee $20; 'A Recreation Passport (park pass) is required for vehicle entry into all state park and forest campgrounds'), read 2026-10-25

values.note: Drinking water from a hand-pump well. Some campsites reach the Lake Michigan beach by a narrow footpath; Marsh Lake Pathway starts in the campground. Small day-use parking area with one picnic table.

facilities.source: https://www.michigan.gov/recsearch/sfcampgroundsa-m/bigknob ('There are vault toilets', 'Potable (drinking) water is available from a hand-pump well', 'Some campsites have direct access to the beach via a narrow footpath', 'A small picnic area is located on the east side of the campground near the day-use parking area'), read 2026-10-25

booking.source: https://www.michigan.gov/recsearch/sfcampgroundsa-m/bigknob ('No reservations. Sites available on a first-come, first-served basis', 'Camping is limited to a 15-day maximum stay') + https://www.michigan.gov/dnr/things-to-do/camping-and-lodging/state-forest-campgrounds/amenity-table ('Reservable at MiDNRReservations.com': no), read 2026-10-25

values.note: 23 sites 'for tent, small trailer and large trailer use'; site #22 is the one pull-through. No length limit posted. One camping unit and six people per site.

sites.source: https://www.michigan.gov/recsearch/sfcampgroundsa-m/bigknob ('There are 23 sites for tent, small trailer and large trailer use. Site #22 is a pull-through site', 'One camping unit and six people are allowed per site') + https://www.michigan.gov/dnr/things-to-do/camping-and-lodging/state-forest-campgrounds/amenity-table (23 campsites), read 2026-10-25

note: Rustic Lake Superior State Forest campground on the Lake Michigan shore among sand dunes, at the dead end of Big Knob Road six miles off US-2 (13.5 miles southwest of Naubinway). Pine Knob and Crow Lake pathways nearby off Big Knob Road. Open all year but the campground and seasonal roads are not plowed. --Claude
summary: DNR page + SF amenity table: 23 sites for tent/small and large trailers, pull-through site #22, $20 at the kiosk + Recreation Passport, no electric, vault toilets, hand-pump water, first-come only, 15-day max (all confirmed, now manual); season open all year already manual; phone 906-293-5900 (Newberry Field Office) matches.
